title: 01. Fundamentals: String Methods — Case Methods
summary: Python strings come with built-in methods — functions you can call directly on a string using dot notation: string.method(). Case methods change the letter casing of strings.

sections.title: CONCEPT EXPLANATION
sections.body:
Python strings come with **built-in methods** — functions you can call directly on a string using dot notation: `string.method()`. Case methods change the **letter casing** of strings.

### Complete Case Methods Reference:

| Method | What it does | Example | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `.upper()` | ALL UPPERCASE | `"hello".upper()` | `"HELLO"` |
| `.lower()` | all lowercase | `"HELLO".lower()` | `"hello"` |
| `.title()` | Title Case | `"hello world".title()` | `"Hello World"` |
| `.capitalize()` | First letter upper, rest lower | `"hELLO".capitalize()` | `"Hello"` |
| `.swapcase()` | Swap upper↔lower | `"HeLLo".swapcase()` | `"hEllO"` |
| `.casefold()` | Aggressive lowercase (Unicode) | `"ß".casefold()` | `"ss"` |

### ⚠️ `capitalize()` vs `title()`:
```python
"hello world".capitalize()  # "Hello world" — only FIRST word
"hello world".title()       # "Hello World" — EVERY word

"HELLO WORLD".capitalize()  # "Hello world" — lowercases rest too!
"hello-world".title()       # "Hello-World" — after hyphen too!
```

### ⚠️ `lower()` vs `casefold()`:
```python
# casefold() is more aggressive — handles Unicode/international chars
"ß".lower()      # "ß"  — German sharp S, stays the same
"ß".casefold()   # "ss" — German: ß is equivalent to ss
# Use casefold() for case-insensitive comparisons!
```

sections.title: 5 EXAMPLES
sections.body:
**What this code covers**

- Case-insensitive user search
- Better title case — handles apostrophes correctly
- Normalize product names to consistent format
- Remember: strings are immutable — methods return NEW strings!
- Real-world: normalizing user-provided data
- Never compare strings directly if casing might differ
- These should ALL find Alice
- Casefold() for international names

**Defines:** `normalize_user()`, `find_user()`, `proper_title()`, `smart_name_case()`, `normalize_product_name()`, `to_slug()`

### Example 1: All Case Methods Demonstrated
```python
text = "hElLo, wOrLd! pYtHoN iS gReAt."

print(f"Original:   {text}")
print(f"upper():    {text.upper()}")
print(f"lower():    {text.lower()}")
print(f"title():    {text.title()}")
print(f"capitalize:{text.capitalize()}")
print(f"swapcase(): {text.swapcase()}")
print(f"casefold(): {text.casefold()}")

# Remember: strings are immutable — methods return NEW strings!
original = "Hello"
upper    = original.upper()
print(f"\nOriginal unchanged: {original}")
print(f"New upper string:   {upper}")

# Chain methods
messy = "  hELLO wOrLD  "
clean = messy.strip().lower().title()
print(f"\nCleaned: '{clean}'")   # 'Hello World'
```

### Example 2: Practical Use — Data Normalization
```python
# Real-world: normalizing user-provided data
user_data = [
    {"name": "ALICE SMITH",    "email": "ALICE@EXAMPLE.COM",   "city": "new delhi"},
    {"name": "bob jones",      "email": "BOB@GMAIL.COM",       "city": "MUMBAI"},
    {"name": "vEeRaBaBu k",    "email": "veera@Example.COM",   "city": "hyderabad"},
]

def normalize_user(user):
    return {
        "name":  user["name"].strip().title(),         # "Alice Smith"
        "email": user["email"].strip().lower(),         # "alice@example.com"
        "city":  user["city"].strip().title(),          # "New Delhi"
    }

normalized = [normalize_user(u) for u in user_data]
print("Normalized user data:")
for u in normalized:
    print(f"  {u['name']:<20} | {u['email']:<30} | {u['city']}")
```

### Example 3: Case-Insensitive Comparisons
```python
# Never compare strings directly if casing might differ
def find_user(users_list, search_name):
    """Case-insensitive user search"""
    search_lower = search_name.lower()
    for user in users_list:
        if user["name"].lower() == search_lower:
            return user
    return None

users = [
    {"name": "Alice Smith",     "role": "admin"},
    {"name": "Veerababu Kumar", "role": "developer"},
    {"name": "Bob Jones",       "role": "manager"},
]

# These should ALL find Alice
for query in ["alice smith", "ALICE SMITH", "Alice Smith", "aLiCe SmItH"]:
    result = find_user(users, query)
    print(f"  Search '{query}': {'Found — ' + result['role'] if result else 'Not found'}")

# casefold() for international names
# German name: "Straße" (contains ß)
name1 = "Straße"
name2 = "strasse"   # German: ß = ss
print(f"\n'{name1}'.casefold() == '{name2}': {name1.casefold() == name2.casefold()}")
# True — casefold handles it correctly
# lower() would give False (ß.lower() == ß, not ss)
```

### Example 4: `title()` Edge Cases and Fixes
```python
# title() has quirks with apostrophes and hyphens
print("it's python".title())       # "It'S Python" ← BUG! apostrophe resets
print("mary-jane".title())         # "Mary-Jane"   ← works well
print("john mcdonald".title())     # "John Mcdonald" ← should be "McDonald"

# Fix the apostrophe issue
import re
def proper_title(text):
    """Better title case — handles apostrophes correctly"""
    return re.sub(r"[A-Za-z]+('[A-Za-z]+)?",
                  lambda m: m.group(0).capitalize(), text)

tests = ["it's a test", "don't stop", "o'reilly's book", "mary-jane watson"]
for t in tests:
    print(f"  '{t}' → '{proper_title(t)}'")

# Handling names like "McGregor", "van der Berg"
def smart_name_case(name):
    parts = name.strip().split()
    result = []
    lowercase_particles = {"van", "der", "de", "la", "le", "di", "da", "von", "zu"}
    for i, part in enumerate(parts):
        if i > 0 and part.lower() in lowercase_particles:
            result.append(part.lower())
        else:
            result.append(part.capitalize())
    return " ".join(result)

names = ["JOHN VAN DER BERG", "MARIA DE SILVA", "JAMES MCGREGOR"]
for n in names:
    print(f"  '{n}' → '{smart_name_case(n)}'")
```

### Example 5: Case Methods in Data Processing
```python
# Processing product names from multiple data sources
raw_products = [
    "LAPTOP DELL INSPIRON 15",
    "phone samsung galaxy s24",
    "TABLET apple iPad PRO",
    "headphones SONY WH-1000XM5",
    "keyboard MECHANICAL rgb",
]

def normalize_product_name(name):
    """Normalize product names to consistent format"""
    words = name.strip().split()
    result = []

    # Known brand names that should stay in specific case
    brands = {
        "dell": "Dell", "samsung": "Samsung", "apple": "Apple",
        "sony": "Sony", "rgb": "RGB", "wh-1000xm5": "WH-1000XM5"
    }

    for word in words:
        lower_word = word.lower()
        if lower_word in brands:
            result.append(brands[lower_word])
        else:
            result.append(word.capitalize())

    return " ".join(result)

print("Normalized Product Names:")
for product in raw_products:
    print(f"  {product:<40} → {normalize_product_name(product)}")

# Create slug (URL-friendly) version
def to_slug(name):
    return normalize_product_name(name).lower().replace(" ", "-")

print("\nURL Slugs:")
for product in raw_products[:3]:
    print(f"  {to_slug(product)}")
```
